score.note: Correctly distinguishes response-dependent expressions—including direct and dynamic placeholder calls—from request-only expressions, with focused classifier and regression tests.
Handles nested reusable callers and wakes blocked runs after cancellation, with focused coverage; its caller detection and wake-up condition are slightly broader than the reference.

It addresses prefix handling and the header-path cases while ensuring generated patches have usable prefixes, but disabling mnemonic prefixes unnecessarily changes the user’s configured diff presentation and the added tests mainly verify command arguments.

Implements the requested ZIP and squashfs symlink behavior, with focused coverage for listing, reading targets, and traversal safety; range reads and a regular ZIP member ending in the link suffix are not directly tested.
Correctly identifies response placeholders in CEL expressions and adds focused coverage for request-only expressions, misleading placeholder text, and direct ph() calls.
Implements reconnect and engine-state reset across SNMP versions, but defers closing failed connections until Gather returns, includes an unrelated test-path change, and the package suite failed.

Implements the requested ZIP and squashfs symlink behavior with safe suffixed names, and adds useful coverage, though ZIP range handling and regular members ending in the link suffix are not directly tested.
Implements the reference-counted close and unlink behavior, protects relisten races and abstract sockets, and adds focused coverage for the requested lifecycle edge cases.
The parser and most diff commands handle mnemonic and custom prefixes well, but stash diffs are not given guaranteed prefixes, and forcing a/b changes the user-requested mnemonic display.
Exemplars are tracked only at commit, leaving an append/compaction race, and ordinary-GC retention fails to clear the appender that can retain removed chunks.
Matches the reference behavior and adds broad, relevant coverage for compaction paths, both appender APIs, replay, chunk reclamation, and concurrent appends.
The recovery implementation closely matches the fix and adds useful coverage, but the package suite fails and the unrelated Gosmi test-path change broadens scope.
Implements `.rclonelink` semantics across ZIP and squashfs with strong range, lookup, collision, and copy-safety tests, though squashfs clash handling is less comprehensive than ZIP’s.

Correctly identifies response-dependent CEL placeholders while preserving request-only retry conditions, with focused coverage for shorthand, direct calls, dynamic names, and successful-response retries.

The reference-counted socket design addresses the listener leak and most sharing and race cases, but repeated Close can return nil instead of the required net.ErrClosed, which also causes the added double-close test to fail.

Implements the requested symlink convention for ZIP and squashfs, including consistent lookup, skip notices, and destination escape coverage; tests are strong but do not directly exercise range/seek behavior or end-to-end symlink recreation.

The caller aggregation change is relevant, but cancelRun now calls SettleRunAfterCancel even when jobs were updated, which can finalize the run before a runner acknowledges cancellation; the added tests do not cover this service-level path.
Matches the reference fix and thoroughly tests exemplar retention, chunk reclamation, replay, both appender APIs, and compaction paths.
Implements robust diff-path parsing and predictable prefixes across the relevant Git commands; the updated command tests are useful, though parser edge-case coverage is not visible here.

Matches the reference fix and covers reference counting, double-close behavior, relisten races, cleanup, and abstract sockets; the tests are thorough, though some cases check file existence or connection setup rather than full continued service.
Implements the requested link behavior consistently for ZIP and squashfs, preserves regular `.rclonelink` files, and adds focused coverage including a destination-escape check.

Preserves reusable callers in Cancelling until their children settle and rechecks blocked runs after cancellation; the readiness recheck is slightly broader than necessary because it runs whenever no jobs were updated.
Fixes staging and broadens header parsing, but disables the user's mnemonic-prefix setting rather than preserving it, and the visible tests mainly check command arguments.
Matches the reference fix and adds focused coverage for reference counting, double closes, relisten races, unlinking, and abstract sockets.

The recovery flow is largely correct, but restoring explicitly configured engine parameters can prevent rediscovery after an engine-ID change, and unrelated test edits plus the failing package suite reduce confidence.
Correctly detects response placeholders from the CEL AST, preserves dynamic-name handling, and adds focused coverage for request-only expressions and response-based retries.
The fix matches the required prefix handling and header-path parsing; the updated tests verify command arguments but provide limited direct coverage of the parsing edge cases.
The SNMP recovery changes match the fix and are tested, but the unrelated MIB loader changes substantially expand the patch’s scope.
Fixes Unix socket cleanup and reference-counted close behavior, handles relisten races and abstract sockets, and adds focused coverage for the stated requirements.

Retention is inferred from the current exemplar-storage index rather than recorded on the series during append and replay, leaving pending-exemplar races and replay-window cases unprotected; ordinary GC also fails to account for chunks released for retained series, and the checkpoint tests can mistake an existing checkpoint for the one they intended to force.

The caller aggregation fix handles nested reusable workflows and the added tests cover acknowledgement and waiter wake-up, but emitting whenever no jobs changed is broader than necessary and should also require a run-status transition.
Correctly distinguishes response-reading and dynamic placeholders from request-only expressions, with strong coverage; the accessor could clone its returned slice to avoid exposing internal state.
Implements cached-connection closure and reconnect-time SNMPv3 state reset, with useful coverage, but includes unrelated test-path changes and the relevant package suite failed.

Keeps reusable callers cancelling until their children settle and emits settled runs to wake concurrency waiters, though it emits on every no-job-update cancellation even when the run status did not change.

Implements link translation and blocks ZIP entries beneath symlinks, but collisions between a translated link name and a regular `.rclonelink` member can make the exposed object depend on archive order.
The patch attempts broad coverage of exemplar retention and chunk release, but the package suite and all hidden tests fail, so the core behavior is not reliably implemented.

Implements the reconnect and engine rediscovery flow with useful coverage, but clears additional USM key state without testing an authenticated request afterward, includes unrelated test edits, and the package suite failed.
The patch does not compile because it uses `io` without importing it, and it treats every `@` path as an abstract socket even on platforms where that is a filesystem path.
The caller-state guard and concurrency wake-up address both reported failures, but nested cancellation still relies on descendant processing order rather than guaranteeing deepest-first handling.
Implements the ZIP and squashfs symlink conventions correctly, with focused coverage for listing, reading, suffix preservation, and archive escape safety; range behavior is not directly tested.
Matches the reference fix and adds focused coverage for request-only expressions, response placeholders, and direct `ph()` calls.

Implements the reference lifecycle fix, including reference-counted cleanup, idempotent close handling, reload-race protection, and abstract-socket safeguards, with focused coverage of the requested cases.

The core ZIP and squashfs symlink handling is solid, but LinkFilter can incorrectly drop a regular member ending in .rclonelink when a regular member with the corresponding unsuffixed name also exists.

The GC retention, chunk release, replay tracking, and tests are strong, but recording exemplars only at commit leaves a compaction race before commit that the reference avoids by marking them during append.
The parser and command-prefix changes address the reported regression and cover key path cases, but the stash diff command is left without the forced parseable prefixes.
The recovery logic closely matches the reference and covers failed field and table gathers, but the package suite failed and the unrelated test-path change broadens scope.

The patch addresses prefix parsing and patch generation, but it unnecessarily disables the user's mnemonic prefixes and the visible tests mostly verify command arguments rather than the parsing edge cases.

Addresses both stuck caller aggregation and concurrency-group release, with strong nested-caller and settled-run tests; it may report unchanged callers as updated and emits an extra run check when no jobs changed.
Implements the prefix handling and header-path parsing comprehensively; the visible test updates verify command arguments but provide limited direct coverage of the parser edge cases.

The retention and chunk-release paths cover the reported restart scenarios well, but checking only committed exemplar storage can miss an exemplar staged in an appender when compaction races with its commit.

The fix covers the main GC paths and tests them thoroughly, but it can miss an accepted exemplar still pending appender commit, and HasExemplarAtOrAfter reads the exemplar slice before acquiring its lock.
